Takes one member of an item into a body whole: eating a loaf, swallowing a pill (16 §9.5). What it holds goes in by the route, as `dose` puts it, and the member is gone. Gives what got in, in millilitres. Refused with `substance.bad_route` and `substance.bad_argument`.

- `who` (entity): The body.
- `what` (entity): The item; one member of a stack is taken.
- `route` (string): How it gets in: `ingest`, `inject`, `skin` or `breath`.

<a id="take-out"></a>
## `take_out`

Takes a thing out of the container it is stowed in or enclosed by (06 §9.2): into the grasp of `to` as `take` does, or with no `to` to where the container is, as `drop` does. Returns where it went. Refused with `item.not_contained`, and as `take` or `drop` is.

- `what` (entity): The thing, wherever it is.
- `to` (entity?, optional): Who takes it into a grasp. Null to put it where the container is.

<a id="teach"></a>
## `teach`

Teaches an entity's mind a piece of know-how (16 §8.5) and raises `know_how_gained`. Gives whether it was new. Refused with `know_how.needs` while something it needs is not known, and `know_how.no_mind`.

- `who` (entity): Who learns.
- `what` (id<know_how>): The know-how.
- `how` (string?, optional): What `know_how_gained` says of how; `taught` if left out.

<a id="think"></a>
## `think`

Makes a mind think at the next batch (09 §3.3). Refused for a character that thinks by no `mind` definition.

- `who` (entity): The character whose mind thinks.

<a id="throw"></a>
## `throw`

Throws an item `who` holds (07 §11.1): it leaves the hand and flies as a body that is the item, with its own mass and cross-section, from where `who` stands toward `at` or along `dir`, and strikes what it meets with its surface named `surface`, through the same delivery as a projectile's; with none, with a blunt blow. Raises `thrown`. Refused with `ranged.not_held`, `ranged.no_surface`, `ranged.no_energy`, `ranged.no_aim`, `ranged.not_in_world` and `ranged.bad_number`.

- `who` (entity?, optional): Who throws. Default `self`.
- `what` (entity): The item thrown: one `who` holds.
- `at` (any, optional): What it is aimed at, as for `shoot`.
- `dir` (any, optional): The direction it is aimed along, as a list of three numbers.
- `part` (part?, optional): The part of the entity aimed at.
- `height` (real?, optional): Metres above the footing of the entity, or the floor of the cell, it is aimed at.
- `energy` (real?, optional): Joules it leaves the hand with.
- `speed` (real?, optional): Metres a second it leaves the hand at, in place of what its energy gives.
- `spread` (real?, optional): Radians of dispersion, as for `shoot`. Default none.
- `surface` (string?, optional): The id of the item's surface it strikes with. Default none: a blunt blow.
- `lob` (bool?, optional): Whether it is sent along the arc that comes down on the aim point. Default false.
- `window` (id<window_kind>?, optional): The kind of reaction window it opens for the entity it is aimed at, as `shoot`'s does (07 §11.2).

<a id="transfer-mind"></a>
## `transfer_mind`

Moves a mind to another entity, with the attributes, pools and tracks seated in it and the control mode, after the hook `mind_transferring` (06 §8.2).

- `from` (entity): Whose mind moves.
- `to` (entity): Where it goes.
- `swap` (bool, optional): True to let a mind that `to` has go the other way; left out, `to` must have none.

<a id="unlearn"></a>
## `unlearn`

Takes a piece of know-how from an entity's mind (16 §8.5) and raises `know_how_lost`. Gives whether it was known.

- `who` (entity): Who forgets.
- `what` (id<know_how>): The know-how.

<a id="use-ability"></a>
## `use_ability`

Uses an ability (08 §5): starts the action one of its grants makes available, through the action runtime, with its cost taken in full and its cooldown started, after the hook `ability_using`. Returns whether the action started; when it did not, `ability_refused` says why (`ability.not_held`, `ability.dormant`, `ability.rank_too_low`, `ability.cooling_down`, `ability.condition`, `ability.cost_short`, `ability.cost_source_gone`, `ability.items_short`, a refusal of the action runtime, or a handler's).

- `who` (entity): Whose ability.
- `ability` (id<ability>): The ability.
- `action` (id<action>?, optional): The action of the grant. Left out, the ability's only grant.
- `params` (any, optional): The action's parameters, a map by name. The grant's own `params` stand in for any of the same name.

<a id="wait"></a>
## `wait`

Occupies an entity doing nothing (03 §13). When the time is over it is free, and asked what to do next.

- `who` (entity): Who waits.
- `time` (real): How long, in seconds of its own time: `"2 s"`.

<a id="wear"></a>
## `wear`

Puts an item on `who` (06 §9.2): it covers the outer parts its `wear` selects, at its layers, and is a layer for hits on them. One member of a stack is split off and worn. Raises `item_leaving` and `item_taking`, then `item_worn`. Returns what is worn. Refused with `item.not_wearable`, `item.no_body`, `item.no_part_to_wear_on`, `item.layer_taken`, what the kernel refuses, and by a handler of either hook.

- `who` (entity): The creature that holds or wears it: it needs a body.
- `what` (entity): The thing, wherever it is.

<a id="work"></a>
## `work`

Starts a recipe, or goes on with it where it is under way, by a worker (16 §8.2): what a work action's held phase does. Checks as `can_make` does against truth, promotes the station, raises the hook `recipe_starting`, uses up the inputs of a new start and raises `recipe_started`. When the work is done the recipe completes and the worker's held action is let go; if the action ends first the work done is kept. Refused with the reasons of `recipe.*`; the worker's held action is then interrupted.

- `who` (entity): Who works.
- `recipe` (any): The recipe: its id, or its qualified id as a text.
- `at` (any, optional): The station: an element or a device. Left out, by hand.
